question.prompt: The sum of the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\) and the least integer greater than or equal to \(x\) is \(5.\) The solution set for \(x\) is

solutions.explanation:
The two selected integers coincide when \(x\) is an integer and are consecutive otherwise, so consider these cases separately.

If \(x\) is an integer, both selected integers equal \(x\). Their sum is \(2x\), an even integer, so it cannot equal \(5\).

If \(x\) is not an integer, let \(n\) be the greatest integer less than \(x\). Then \(n<x<n+1\), and the least integer greater than \(x\) is \(n+1\). Thus
\[
n+(n+1)=5,
\]
which gives \(n=2\). Hence \(2<x<3\).

Conversely, every \(x\) strictly between \(2\) and \(3\) has the selected integers \(2\) and \(3\), whose sum is \(5\). The endpoints give sums \(4\) and \(6\), respectively. Therefore the solution set is \(\{x\mid 2<x<3\}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Separate integer and noninteger inputs
